title: ‘धन–महिमा’ कवितामा प्रस्तुत वैदिक दर्शन  {Vedic Philosophies in ‘Dhan-Mahima’}
nepali: प्रस्तुत अनुसन्धानात्मक लेखमा लेखनाथ पौड्यालको ‘धन–महिमा’ कवितामा प्रस्तुत वैदिक दर्शनका मूलभूत मान्यताहरूको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । धनलाई सर्वस्व ठानेर यसकोे पछि लागी धन थुपारेर मानिसलाई पारमार्थिकसरख नमिल्ने, जगत्को हितमा उपयोग गर्नुपर्ने धनप्रति मानिस आसक्त भई लागेर मोक्ष मार्गमा पुग्न नसकिने, प्रवृत्त मार्गमा लागेर बन्धन तथा दुःखमा मात्र पाइने, पारमार्थिक सुख नमिल्ने कर्म शुभकर्म नहुने, जति धन भए पनि सन्तुष्टि नहुने र अज्ञानताका कारण मानिस निवृत्तिमार्गमा नभई प्रवृत्तिमार्गमा लागेका जस्ता विषयहरू वैदिक दर्शनका मान्यतामा आधारित देखिन्छन् । कवितामा धनको महिमा गायन गरिए पनि अन्तर्यमा धैर्य गर्नुपर्ने, पारमार्थिक सत्य र सुखको खोजीमा लाग्नुपर्नेजस्ता वैदिक षड्दर्शनका विचारहरू कवितामा व्यक्त भएका छन् । सामग्री सङ्कलनमा पुस्तकालय विधिको प्रयोग गरिएको यस लेखमा प्राथमिक स्रोत सामग्रीको रूपमा ‘लालित्य भाग १’ कविता सङ्ग्रहमा सङ्गृहीत ‘धन–महिमा’ कविता र द्वितीय स्रोतका रूपमा वैदिक दर्शनसँग सम्बन्धित ग्रन्थहरू, समालोचनात्मक कृतिहरू, लेखहरू तथा अनुसन्धनात्मक लेखहरूलाई लिइएको छ । यहाँ वैदिक षड्दर्शनहरू (साङ्ख्य, योग, न्याय, वैशेषिक, मीमांसा र वेदान्त दर्शन)का लोभ, मोह, दुःख, मोक्ष, निवृत्तिमार्ग, अविद्या, माया, बन्धनका सम्बन्धमा रहेका मान्यताहरूलाई आधार मानेर कविताशंहरूलाई दृष्टान्त दिएर पाठपरक विधिमार्फत विश्लेषण गरिएको छ ।
american_english: In this research article, the fundamental assumptions of Vedic philosophy presented in Lekhnath Paudyal's poem "Dhan-Mahima" have been analyzed. Themes such as the idea that by considering wealth to be everything and running after it and accumulating it, a person cannot attain the ultimate spiritual goal just like that, that a person attached to wealth cannot use it for the welfare of the world and reach the path of liberation, that by following the path of worldly activity one finds only bondage and suffering, that ultimate spiritual happiness is not attained, that actions do not become virtuous actions, that no matter how much wealth one has there is no satisfaction, and that because of ignorance people remain on the path of worldly activity rather than the path of renunciation appear to be based on the assumptions of Vedic philosophy. Although the poem sings the glory of wealth, ideas of the Vedic six systems of philosophy, such as the need to maintain patience inwardly and to engage in the search for ultimate truth and happiness, have been expressed in the poem. In this article, which used the library method for the collection of materials, the poem "Dhan-Mahima" included in the poetry collection "Lalitya Part 1" was taken as the primary source material, and texts related to Vedic philosophy, critical works, articles, and research articles were taken as secondary sources. Here, taking as a basis the assumptions found in the Vedic six systems of philosophy (Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta philosophy) concerning greed, attachment, suffering, liberation, the path of renunciation, ignorance, illusion, and bondage, the verses of the poem have been analyzed through a text-based method by giving illustrations.

informal_english: This research article has a look at the basic ideas of Vedic philosophy in Lekhnath Paudyal's poem "Dhan-Mahima". Stuff like thinking wealth is everything and chasing after it and piling it up means you can't really reach the ultimate spiritual goal, that someone who's hung up on wealth can't use it for the good of the world and get onto the path of liberation, that sticking to the path of worldly activity just lands you in bondage and suffering, that you don't get ultimate spiritual happiness, that your actions don't turn into good deeds, that no matter how much money you've got you're never satisfied, and that because of ignorance people stay on the path of worldly activity instead of the path of renunciation all seem to be based on the ideas of Vedic philosophy. Even though the poem praises the glory of wealth, ideas from the Vedic six systems of philosophy show up in it too, like needing to stay patient on the inside and to go looking for ultimate truth and happiness. This article used the library method to gather materials, taking the poem "Dhan-Mahima" from the poetry collection "Lalitya Part 1" as the main source, and texts about Vedic philosophy, critical works, articles, and research articles as secondary sources. Here, using as a basis the ideas found in the Vedic six systems of philosophy (Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta philosophy) about greed, attachment, suffering, liberation, the path of renunciation, ignorance, illusion, and bondage, the poem's verses have been analysed through a text-based method with examples.
